description: Turkish vocabulary register audit list. 'formal' = Ottoman-era Arabic/Persian loan or stiff written construction (or, in reform_words_overcorrected, an öz Türkçe coinage that lost to an older loan in daily speech); 'preferred' = what Turkish speakers actually say in everyday conversation. Severity: 'high' = dead in modern speech, swap wherever it appears; 'medium' = alive in official/news/academic registers but stiff in dialogue — swap in beginner content; 'low' = both registers common, context call. Guiding principle: target what people SAY, not language-reform ideology. Legal/official set phrases quoted as such are exempt. Used by scripts/audit-tr-register.cjs.

bureaucratic_verbs.rationale: Ottoman bureaucratic verb + etmek/olmak compounds. Most have a single dominant everyday equivalent. A few survive as euphemisms or in fossilized official phrases — see notes.

entries.note: müracaat survives on old signage ('Müracaat' = reception desk); nobody uses the verb in speech
the noun talep is alive in economics (arz-talep) and customer-service talk; the verb is stiff in dialogue

entries.rom: tanzim etmek → düzenlemek (to arrange, draw up)
entries.note: 'fatura tanzimi' is pure officialese; only historical 'tanzim satış' keeps the word visible
the closing 'arz ederim' is the standard formula in official correspondence and military speech — exempt when quoted as such
'Nerede oturuyorsun?' is the only natural spoken form; ikamet belongs on residence-permit forms

entries.rom: vefat etmek → ölmek (to pass away / to die)
entries.note: NOT a dead word — vefat etmek is the standard polite euphemism for a person's death; keep it when softness/respect is the point, teach ölmek as the plain verb
dated periphrastic variant; imzalamak is universal
legal/tax contexts (beyanname, gümrük beyanı) are exempt — there beyan is the technical term
fine in essays; in dialogue it sounds like a news anchor. The noun ifade is alive (police statement, 'ifade vermek')
the exclamation 'Tebrikler!' is fully alive and should never be flagged; only the verb sounds stiff ('seni tebrik ederim' vs 'kutlarım')

entries.rom: teşrif etmek → gelmek (to honor with one's presence / to come)
entries.note: survives in hyper-polite hospitality ('teşrif edin') and in irony; never neutral

entries.rom: tekabül etmek → karşılık gelmek (to correspond to)
entries.note: academic register; heard in lectures, not conversation
the noun ihtar is alive as a legal notice (ihtarname) and a football booking; the verb is dead in speech
official-document contexts exempt; occasionally jocular in speech ('tasdik ediyorum!')
faydalanmak is also Arabic-derived but fully alive — target usage, not etymology
diplomacy/news register; müzakere as noun is standard there
colloquially alive for verbal quarrels, especially among older speakers ('münakaşa etmeyin') — context call

entries.rom: ibraz etmek → göstermek (to present, show a document)
entries.note: official signage ('kimlik ibrazı zorunludur') is exempt when quoted

entries.rom: ifa etmek → yerine getirmek (to fulfill, perform)

entries.note: icra is alive as the debt-enforcement office ('icraya vermek') and in music (a piece is 'icra edilir') — exempt those senses
news/economics register; istihdam as noun (employment) is the standard technical term
the noun tetkik is fully alive in medicine ('tetkikler istendi' = tests were ordered) — exempt that sense

entries.rom: iştigal etmek → uğraşmak (to be occupied with)
entries.note: survives jocularly in mock-formal 'ne işle iştigal ediyorsunuz?'
older speakers only; blessing formula 'Allah muvaffak etsin' survives regionally

entries.rom: zuhur etmek → ortaya çıkmak (to appear, emerge)
entries.note: sometimes used jocularly for someone showing up unannounced — that use is intentional register play

entries.rom: tahsil etmek → toplamak (to collect money) / okumak (to be educated)
entries.note: two senses: tahsilat is alive in payments; 'tahsil görmek' for education is dated — 'okumak' is what people say

abstract_nouns.rationale: Ottoman abstract nouns with everyday equivalents. Several remain colloquially alive in set phrases or specific senses — do not blanket-swap without checking notes.

entries.note: 'bu hususta' is pure bureaucratese; speech says 'bu konuda'
'lüzum yok' lingers with older speakers, but 'gerek yok' is the default everywhere
do not confuse with the adjective malum, which is alive (see quantifiers_adjectives)
survives jocularly in greetings ('ahval nasıl?') — intentional flavor, exempt there
alive among older speakers and in 'hadise çıkarmak' (to make a scene); olay is the neutral default
the connector 'neticede' is still common in speech — exempt; the bare noun is dated
older speakers; amaç won
'vasıtasıyla' → 'aracılığıyla' or plain 'üzerinden'; older speakers still say vasıta for vehicles
colloquially alive ('vaziyet ne?', 'vaziyeti idare et') — context call, do not blanket-swap
fully alive ('mesele yok', 'para meselesi', 'mesele şu ki') — only swap if sentence is otherwise plain-neutral
kabiliyetli is still colloquial; yetenek is the neutral default (yetenekli, yetenek avcısı)
alive on the traffic sign 'mecburi istikamet' and in dolmuş/military talk — exempt those; elsewhere yön
the adjective mecbur is fully colloquial ('mecburum', 'mecbur muyum?') — never flag mecbur itself
'ehemmiyet verme' heard only from older speakers
alive with older speakers and in moralizing tone ('vazifen bu'); görev is neutral
older speakers and religious-school contexts only
set phrase 'sıhhatler olsun' (after a haircut/bath) is fully alive — exempt; elsewhere sağlık
Emniyet as the police force (proper noun) and 'emniyet kemeri' (seatbelt) are standard — exempt those senses
menfaatçi (self-serving person) is alive colloquially; the bare noun is formal
detay (French loan) is the true spoken default; ayrıntı is the neutral written word; teferruatlı = older speakers
münasebetsiz (rude, out of line) is fully alive — exempt; 'ne münasebet!' (certainly not!) is also alive
'işin mahiyeti' is bureaucratic/legal boilerplate
şahsen (personally) is fully alive — exempt; şahıs in dialogue sounds like a police report
alive in 'bedelli askerlik', transfer fees, and 'bedelini ödemek' (pay the price) — context call
parenting-literature and school-circular word; at home everyone says anne baba(m)
'mesela' is universal and untouchable; bare 'misal' as a sentence-initial filler is actually colloquial-jocular — context call
'hakkaten' (really) is fully alive colloquially; hakikat itself carries literary/religious flavor — context call

time_words.rationale: Ottoman temporal adverbs and postpositional phrases. Modern speech uses sonra, önce, sırasında, -ken and plain hemen/genelde.

entries.note: 'bir müddet sonra' survives with older speakers; süre is the default everywhere else
the suffix -ken ('yemek yerken') is the most natural spoken option of all
alive in set forms — evvela (first of all), evvelsi gün (day before yesterday), and rural/older speech; standalone 'beş sene evvel' sounds dated-flavorful, not wrong
occasionally jocular in educated banter; otherwise dead
'günü müteakip' is pure officialese
'üç gün zarfında' is bureaucratic; zarf = envelope is a different, fully alive word
journalistic and frequently misused; fine in reports, stiff in dialogue
alive as a sharp command ('Derhal buraya gel!') — intentional emphasis; neutral speech uses hemen
alive in slogans and mottos ('daima ileri') and posh speech; hep/her zaman are the conversational defaults
fully alive ('vaktim yok', 'namaz vakti', 'tam vaktinde') — both registers common, no swap needed; context call only

entries.rom: bugün itibarıyla → bugünden başlayarak / bugün olarak (as of)
entries.note: '-den itibaren' ('saat beşten itibaren') is fully alive — never flag it; only '-ı itibarıyla' is the stiff construction

quantifiers_adjectives.rationale: Ottoman adjectives and quantifiers. Beware: several survive colloquially as emphatic or jocular flavor (mühim, malum, külliyen) — those are low severity by design.

entries.note: 'ekseriyetle' heard only from older speakers
'Kafi!' as a dramatic interjection survives (dated-theatrical); attributive use is stiff
still colloquially alive for emphasis ('en mühimi bu', 'mühim değil' among older speakers) — do NOT mark high; context call
fully alive colloquially ('malum sebeplerden', discourse marker 'malum ya...') — context call only
alive in semi-formal 'mevcut durumda' and classroom roll count ('mevcut 30'); in plain speech 'X var' beats 'X mevcuttur'
news word ('münferit olaylar'); nobody says it conversationally
fully alive in real estate ('müstakil ev' = detached house) — exempt that sense
news register; heard in deliberately dramatic speech ('durum vahim')
alive for emphasis among educated speakers ('elzem değil') — medium, not high
survives jocularly ('bilumum akraba') — intentional humor is exempt
fossil on old signage ('umumi tuvalet'); 'umumiyetle' is dated for genellikle/genelde
older speakers; 'hususi araç' long replaced by 'özel araç'
survives as jocular-emphatic exaggeration ('mütemadiyen şikayet ediyor') — that use is intentional
alive in emphatic denial ('külliyen yalan!') — colloquial flavor, exempt when emphatic
older speakers only
literary but heard in argumentative speech ('aşikar ki'); 'ortada' is the punchy spoken option
alive as a posh/dated exclamation ('Fevkalade!') — intentional register play; neutral speech says harika
as 'except' ('İstanbul müstesna') legal-archaic = high; as praise ('müstesna güzellik') literary/ad copy — that sense is deliberate
the contraction 'vesaire (vs.)' is fully alive — never flag it; bare 'sair' is legal boilerplate
unlike lüzum, lüzumsuz is still colloquially alive ('lüzumsuz konuşma') — context call
set phrase 'ehven-i şer' (lesser evil) alive among educated speakers — exempt

conjunctions_connectors.rationale: Connectors are where register play is most intentional — lakin, velhasıl, keza survive as deliberate flavor. Only the true fossils (binaenaleyh, mamafih, mucibince) are unconditional swaps.

entries.note: common in writing; in speech sounds bookish, though some educated speakers use it deliberately
alive in speech for poetic/emphatic effect ('lakin unutma...') — intentional flavor; do not flag in dialogue meant to be expressive

entries.rom: nitekim → zaten/gerçekten de (indeed, as a matter of fact)
entries.note: journalistic but genuinely used by educated speakers — medium, not high
survives as educated-jocular one-word agreement ('Keza.') — intentional; otherwise dead
fine in writing and formal emphasis; bile is the spoken default. Unrelated homograph dâhi (genius) is a different word
'yahut da' as an afterthought filler is alive for some speakers; as a plain 'or' it reads dated
survives as a deliberate drawl ('veyahut da...'); plain use is dated
alive but formal-leaning; plain -se/-sa with no conjunction at all is the most natural spoken conditional

entries.rom: buna binaen → bundan dolayı (based on, owing to)

entries.note: legal fossil; even gereğince is formal — plain '-e göre' in speech
jocular educated use is alive ('yorgunluk hasebiyle') — intentional humor exempt
colloquially alive as a storyteller's wrap-up; 'velhasıl kelam' is jocular set phrase — context call, often intentional
jocular revival among columnists; not conversational

entries.rom: gerek A gerekse B → hem A hem B (both A and B)
entries.note: fine in writing and speeches; hem...hem (de) is the spoken pair

formal_constructions.rationale: Grammatical constructions of official/academic prose. Standard in reports and news — flag them only in conversational example sentences. Quoted legal text is exempt.

entries.note: the -maktadır progressive is standard in academic/news prose — flag only in dialogue and beginner sentences
'lazım' is the most colloquial of all ('gitmem lazım')

entries.rom: polis tarafından durduruldu → polis durdurdu (the police stopped [him])
entries.note: agentless passive is fine when the agent is unknown/irrelevant; it is the explicit 'X tarafından' in dialogue that sounds like a police report

entries.rom: gelmediği takdirde → gelmezse (if he doesn't come)
entries.note: contract/legal texts exempt when quoted

entries.rom: ödemek kaydıyla → ödemek şartıyla / öderse (provided that)
entries.note: kaydıyla is contract language; şartıyla is neutral, plain conditional -irse is most spoken

entries.rom: söz konusu araç → bu araç (the vehicle in question → this vehicle)
entries.note: the set phrase 'söz konusu bile olamaz!' (out of the question!) is fully alive — exempt; only the determiner use is bureaucratic
ironic-jocular use is alive among educated speakers; neutral use is dead

entries.rom: rapora istinaden → rapora dayanarak (based on the report)
görüşmek maksadıyla → görüşmek için (in order to meet)
entries.note: maksat itself survives colloquially in 'maksat muhabbet (olsun)' — exempt that idiom
bureaucratic filler; usually deletable entirely

entries.rom: konuyla ilgili olarak → konu hakkında (regarding the topic)
entries.note: 'ile ilgili' without 'olarak' is fine in speech; the 'olarak' tail is the bureaucratic part

entries.rom: ne şekilde → nasıl (in what manner → how)
gitmek durumunda kaldım → gitmek zorunda kaldım (I had to go)
entries.note: both heard; 'durumunda' leans corporate-polite, 'zorunda' is the natural spoken default

reform_words_overcorrected.rationale: Öz Türkçe coinages pushed in education/writing that never displaced the older (usually Arabic) loan in daily speech. The reform word is 'formal' here. Target what people say, not purist ideology — but note where the coinage owns a domain (math class, software UI, urbanism).

entries.note: yanıt owns exams and software UI ('yanıtla'); in conversation everyone says 'cevap ver'
sözcük belongs to grammar class and linguistics; kelime is universal in speech
kent is alive in compounds and municipal branding ('kentsel dönüşüm', 'kent konseyi') — exempt those; plain speech says şehir
'imkânı yok' / 'imkânsız' are the living idioms; olanak reads as newspaper prose
olasılık owns math class; conversation says 'ihtimal vermiyorum', 'düşük ihtimal'
'şart değil', 'tek şartla' are the spoken idioms; koşul is fine in written/technical prose — context call
bureaucratic öz Türkçe found on memos ('ivedilikle'); nobody says ivedi — acil is universal (Acil = ER)
literature-class word; speech uses anlatmak or tarif etmek
both alive; hayat dominates speech and set phrases ('hayatım', 'hayatta olmaz', 'iş hayatı') — context call
art-criticism register; eser is what people say ('eser miktarda' is a separate live idiom)
both fine — örneğin is written-neutral, mesela is the spoken default; only swap in casual dialogue
